claim_gate.reason: The decoder class is explicit and polynomial, but neither inverse-polynomial uniform-legal target coverage nor exponential assignment decay is proved.

decoder_contract.branching: allow offsets in [-1,1] on 2 ceil(log2 n) selected coordinates and zero elsewhere
decoder_contract.finite_controls: larger-n random-witness sweeps plus exact full-Boolean-cube uniform-legal target censuses on preregistered smaller rows
decoder_contract.input: independent uniform DCP labels and an independent uniform subset-sum target conditioned on existence of a Boolean witness
decoder_contract.list_size: (2q+1)^(c ceil(log2 n)); carry slicing adds at most n+O(1)
decoder_contract.output: enumerate selected nearest-plane paths, decode each marker-one vector, and verify the original modular subset-sum equation
decoder_contract.selector: rank exact target-independent LLL Gram-Schmidt rows by public Rademacher variance divided by squared rounding margin

falsifiers_triggered: The preregistered carry-sliced logarithmic-coordinate cell union has held-out witness coverage 8.13802e-05 at n=56 and log2 slope -0.305721 per n; this is finite decay, not an asymptotic theorem.
summary: Tested 27 public-risk-selected logarithmic-coordinate decoders through n=56; tail witness coverage standard/carry=4.06901e-05/8.13802e-05, carry log2 slope=-0.305721. The list-size and source-transfer theorems are proved; asymptotic coverage is open.

transfer_theorem.proof: Each uncovered legal target contains at least one rejected assignment, and each covered target contains at least one accepted assignment; count targets against assignments and divide by the legal-target count.
transfer_theorem.statement: For every fixed label row, if q is accepted-assignment mass, p is uniform-legal covered-target mass, and mu is mean legal-fiber multiplicity, then max(0,1-mu(1-q)) <= p <= min(1,mu q).
